steps.name: TF activity with decoupleR ulm on CollecTRI regulons
caveats: A prior network is the same for every tissue: a regulator that acts only in kidney can be missed, and a target silent in kidney adds noise. State this in the report.
A TF activity score is an inference from target behaviour, not a measurement of TF protein or of binding; the TF's own transcript need not change.
steps.context: 12 samples total. A regulatory network cannot be inferred from this expression matrix — mutual-information network inference needs on the order of one hundred samples — so a prior knowledge network is the only sound source of regulons here. VIPER and ARACNe are not available in this environment; decoupleR's linear model on a prior network is the substitute. Both CollecTRI human 2.0 and DoRothEA human were present in the reference store at planning time.

plan.title: Aldosterone vs vehicle kidney DE + TF activity
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single gene-level count matrix (12000 genes x 12 samples, counts.csv) from Salmon plus a 12-row metadata table naming condition (aldosterone-treated vs vehicle control), human kidney, 6 vs 6, unpaired, single batch. The research question has two parts: which genes change between treated and control, and which transcription factors sit behind those changes.

T1S1 runs sample-structure QC on the raw counts (blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) so that any outlier or unexpected grouping is visible before a model is fitted. T1S2 fits the negative binomial model with an explicit reference level (control as denominator) and tests the contrast condition: treated vs control with the DESeq2 Wald test, apeglm shrinkage for ranking, independent filtering on and BH adjustment at alpha 0.05. One caveat is structural and carried through the plan and report: the counts are a gene-level table from Salmon with no per-sample quant.sf files and no average transcript-length table in the inputs, so the length offset cannot be reconstructed; the model is fitted on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and a shift in isoform usage can therefore appear as differential expression. tximport must not be run on a gene-level table. T1S2b repeats the test with the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same counts and design as an independent robustness check, since 6 per group is at the low-to-middle end where the two tools disagree on some genes; the intersection is the high-confidence set.

T2S2 answers the second half of the question. With 12 samples, a network cannot be inferred from this expression matrix — mutual-information network inference needs on the order of a hundred samples — so TF activity is estimated from a prior knowledge network only: decoupleR's univariate linear model on the Wald statistic of every tested gene (not only the significant ones), against the signed human CollecTRI regulons, keeping the mode of regulation so a repressor's targets lower the score, with a minimum regulon size of 5. The environment holds CollecTRI 2.0 for human and DoRothEA human as the documented alternative. T1S3 assembles the report with the fit diagnostics, the p-value histogram, the two-method overlap, the TF activity table, and the reproducibility record.

No enrichment step is planned: the question asks for genes and transcription factors, not pathways.

Then the TF activity table with the regulon collection and version, the number of regulators tested, and the leading targets behind the top TFs, read as inference from a tissue-agnostic prior network. State plainly the length-offset limitation of the delivered Salmon gene-level counts and what it means for interpretation. Close with the reproducibility record: sessionInfo, seed, package versions, and the regulon collection version.
steps.context: Human kidney, 6 aldosterone-treated vs 6 vehicle control, single batch, 12000 genes profiled.
acceptance_criteria: Method, package versions, design, contrast, thresholds, number tested and number DE are stated before any gene table
MA plot, dispersion plot and p-value histogram are present with a one-line reading of each
Gene table ranked by shrunken log2 fold change, carrying the unshrunken estimate and lfcSE alongside
DESeq2/edgeR counts and intersection size reported; intersection named the high-confidence set
TF activity section names the regulon collection and version and states that activity is inferred from a prior network, not measured
The Salmon length-offset limitation is stated explicitly
Reproducibility record (sessionInfo, seed, package versions, regulon collection version) is stored with the results
constraints: Rank genes and draw plots on the shrunken log2 fold change; keep p-values from the unshrunken fit
Do not present the union of the two DE methods as the result
Do not add pathway or gene set enrichment — the research question asks for genes and transcription factors only
caveats: With 12 samples the analysis is adequately but not generously powered; report effect sizes with their standard errors rather than fold change alone

grounding.reason: No rule covers the report step as a whole; its settings are copied from the returned skeleton and the cited reporting claims

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

steps.method: Blind VST, PCA on top variable genes, sample distance heatmap
